evidence.exact_quote: Mutation-capable attempts require a valid runtime safe point before dispatch.

items.impact: Implementations can disagree on who certifies a safe point, how freshness is established, and whether a concurrent mutation invalidates it before dispatch.
items.statement: PG-044 requires a valid safe point before mutation-capable dispatch but does not define the validity predicate, authority, persistence identity, expiry, or atomic check-and-dispatch boundary.
items.title: Safe-point validity has no canonical oracle

evidence.exact_quote: UI and projections must not collapse blocked outcomes into failures for policy, FileSafe, side-effect confirmation, or auth-refresh blocks.

items.impact: A run that is simultaneously blocked and encounters an execution failure can be projected differently across consumers, producing misleading recovery actions and inconsistent terminal state.
items.statement: The blocked-versus-failed distinction is explicit, but PG-045 gives no precedence or transition rule for concurrent, nested, superseded, or post-block failures.
items.title: Blocked and failed collision semantics are undefined

evidence.exact_quote: Scheduler correctness must use event-driven authoritative wakeups rather than timer polling.

items.impact: Lost, duplicated, reordered, delayed, or partitioned wakeups can strand work or dispatch it multiple times without violating the stated no-polling rule.
items.statement: PG-046 forbids polling but does not specify durable delivery, deduplication, ordering, replay, backpressure, offline recovery, or observability for authoritative wakeups.
items.title: Event-driven wakeups lack delivery and recovery semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Wizard flows must persist blocked as a canonical state distinct from attention_required.

items.impact: Writers and projections may diverge on entering, resuming, superseding, expiring, or clearing blocked state, despite sharing the same stored label.
items.statement: PG-047 establishes persistence and distinct identity but omits the state machine, transition authority, idempotency rules, and recovery behavior for blocked wizard flows.
items.title: Wizard blocked state lacks transition ownership

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime integrity acceptance requires graph stop, safe-point enforcement, blocked/failed UI separation, event-driven scheduling, and real wizard blocked handling.

items.impact: A plan-index or migration pass can leave each runtime property untested while the composite acceptance unit remains formally addressable.
items.statement: PG-048 names five runtime-integrity outcomes, but its validation surfaces are plan migration and indexing rather than executable oracles, fixtures, or failure injections for those outcomes.
items.title: Runtime integrity acceptance has no runtime proof

evidence.exact_quote: The post-edit sweep must verify backend, runtime, storage, and provider docs align on scheduler, blocked, remediation, and recovery vocabulary.

items.impact: The mandatory sweep can produce incompatible pass results depending on which document or token set a reviewer treats as authoritative.
items.statement: PG-049 requires alignment across document families but does not bind an authoritative vocabulary schema, complete consumer inventory, comparison algorithm, or durable sweep receipt.
items.title: Mandatory vocabulary sweep lacks an authority and receipt

evidence.exact_quote: The post-edit sweep must verify chat, dashboard, Final GUI, wizard, and scheduler/remediation GUI surfaces model blocked state consistently.

items.impact: Surfaces may share a label while differing in stale-state indication, available actions, assistive semantics, translated copy, or offline recovery cues.
items.statement: PG-050 names GUI consumers but does not define a canonical view model or fixtures for stale projections, offline state, accessibility, localization, remediation actions, and blocked-to-resumed transitions.
items.title: GUI blocked-state consistency is not falsifiable

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime packet verification must align terminology across executor, contracts, storage, UI, and providers, forbid lexical dispatch, preserve blocked semantics, and expose queue analysis in a canonical UI surface.

items.impact: Packet producers and consumers can pass different subsets of the composite rule, and untrusted or legacy terms can reach dispatch or UI without a single schema-level rejection point.
items.statement: PG-051 combines terminology, dispatch, blocked semantics, and queue visibility but does not define the packet schema version, exhaustive caller/consumer set, lexical-dispatch detector, or canonical UI binding.
items.title: Runtime packet gate is composite but not schema-bound

evidence.exact_quote: Packet verification must reject incomplete recovery or unsafe section targeting, including trailing-subsection replace_section plans without a later same-level anchor.

items.impact: Malformed headings, duplicate anchors, concurrent document edits, or partial writes can target or replace the wrong content while satisfying a narrow later-anchor check.
items.statement: PG-052 identifies one unsafe trailing-subsection case but leaves heading parsing, selector normalization, untrusted input rejection, document-version preconditions, atomic replacement, and rollback unspecified.
items.title: Section repair safety is narrower than the mutation surface

evidence.exact_quote: Scheduler packet alignment must preserve canonical event-name precedence, forbid post-lock graph degradation, remove lexical dispatch, and honor wake/restore overrides.

items.impact: Conflicting canonical names, aliases, wakeups, and restore events can select different paths across implementations, especially during migration or concurrent recovery.
items.statement: PG-053 asserts precedence and overrides without giving the ordered precedence table, alias sunset/version rules, collision handling, or restore-versus-wake race semantics.
items.title: Scheduler alignment lacks an ordered precedence contract

evidence.exact_quote: Scheduler alignment must keep blocked outcomes distinct from failures in UI/projections.

items.impact: Builders have no discretion to render a blocked scheduler outcome as a generic failure, preventing one class of misleading UI state.
items.statement: PG-054 states an unambiguous blocked-versus-failed UI projection invariant and repeats it as a negative constraint.
items.title: Scheduler UI state distinction is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Packet verification must fail if primary or summary docs retain runtime contradictions in dispatch, blocked payloads, identity, clarification state, command IDs, or hidden retries.

items.impact: A contradiction can be detected without a deterministic answer for which source wins, who adjudicates it, or whether the packet remains blocked after one side changes.
items.statement: PG-055 mandates failure on contradictions but does not define primary-versus-summary authority, canonical conflict precedence, adjudication ownership, or a recovery and revalidation protocol.
items.title: Contradiction detection has no adjudication contract

evidence.exact_quote: The sole canonical blocked payload field is allowed_action_ids[]; deprecated names are defects outside deprecation, migration, or gate-detection text.

items.impact: Packet producers, storage, contracts, HITL, FileSafe, and publishing consumers have a single canonical field and narrowly bounded legacy-text exceptions.
items.statement: PG-056 defines allowed_action_ids[] as the sole canonical blocked payload field and limits deprecated field names to deprecation, migration, or defect-detection contexts.
items.title: Blocked payload field authority is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime recovery sweeps must fail deprecated blocked payload fields, stale append-only contradictions, analysis_id queue identity, and blocked-reason-as-failure-class modeling.

items.impact: Known stale forms may survive because the listed plan migration and index validators do not themselves prove runtime packet, queue identity, or failure-class behavior.
items.statement: PG-057 enumerates four defect families but provides no fixture corpus, scan scope, parser rules, runtime receipt, or per-family pass/fail oracle beyond generic plan migration and index validation.
items.title: Recovery canonicalization sweep is not executable

evidence.exact_quote: Coverage blockers `cov-034`, `cov-511`, and `cov-526` require owner-definition records before

items.impact: Records can contain the required fields yet be created, amended, retired, or accepted by inconsistent actors, allowing blocker status to drift across gates.
items.statement: PG-058 gives a strong owner-definition field set and placeholder scan, but does not define the record schema location, identifier uniqueness, lifecycle transitions, approval authority, or gate-consumption receipt.
items.title: Owner-definition records lack lifecycle governance

evidence.exact_quote: - python3 scripts/pm-plan-index.py validate
- python3 scripts/pm-bootstrap-ledger-validate.py Plans/ledgers/v2/pldg-20260618-001-prd-planning-wizard

items.impact: The compile-ready gate can claim a context-aware zero-incomplete scan while its declared validation surfaces do not identify a validator that scans all required artifacts or tests the exception lifecycle.
items.statement: PG-059 specifies extensive zero-incomplete behavior and exact user-approved exception metadata, but its validation_surfaces name only plan-index and ledger validation, not the promised cross-artifact context-aware incomplete-content validator or falsifiable fixtures.
items.title: Zero-incomplete gate has no declared enforcing validator

evidence.exact_quote: gate is blocked, Approve And Build remains disabled and the disabled reason lists currently open blocker families
gui_related: false

items.impact: GUI assurance and downstream indexing can omit a unit that directly governs the enabled state and explanatory copy of Approve And Build.
items.statement: PG-060 is classified gui_related=false even though its canonical contract requires Planning Wizard disabled-state truthfulness and exact user-visible disabled reasons for Approve And Build.
items.title: Implementation-readiness gate is misclassified as non-GUI

evidence.exact_quote:
live generated-project validators exist. A successful run-gates result cannot be reported as PASS evidence for
  tombstoned or manual-pending gates unless a validator explicitly targets that gate.

items.impact: A broad green run-gates result cannot falsely close tombstoned or manual-pending gate obligations without gate-specific validator evidence.
items.statement: PG-061 explicitly distinguishes reserved tombstones and manual-pending traceability gates from script-enforced gates and forbids treating untargeted run-gates success as PASS evidence.
items.title: Manual and tombstoned gate evidence boundary is explicit

Reviewed PG-052 through PG-056 across structural mutation safety, scheduler precedence, GUI projection truth, contradiction authority, payload schema migration, untrusted input, concurrency, rollback, and falsifiability.
